newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: First Japanese broadcaster launched in Singapore.
newsitem.headline: First Japanese broadcaster launched in Singapore.

text.p: Singapore invited more Japanese broadcasters on Monday to come to the city state as part of its effort to become a major international multi-media centre.
"I hope other Japanese broadcast companies will also be persuaded to come," Information Minister George Yeo said at the launch of Japan Entertainment Television (JET TV) in Singapore.
"The official launch of JET TV...marks another milestone in our efforts to make Singapore a major international multi-media centre," Yeo said.
A government statement said JET TV, which began operations in March, was the first in Asia to broadcast programmes 24 hour a day in four languages.
From Singapore, JET TV will offer drama, variety, animation, documentary, sports and music ranging from China to Australia and from Japan to India.

To become a regional broadcasting centre, Singapore has upgraded its infrastructure, attracting international broadcasters including Asia Business News, Discovery, ESPN, Star Sports, HBO, MTV and Sony Pictures.
The government was also training more young Singaporeans in the multi-media industry to meet the increasing need for skilled manpower, Yeo said.
"In essence, what we are trying to do is to create a total environment for the development and the growth of the multi-media industry in Singapore," he said.
